title: GitHub Apps, tokens and rulesets
bridge: A GitHub App installation token is like a one-hour API key that acts as the bot. Except: it is minted from a private key each time, so there is nothing static to paste. Each token can be narrowed to one repo and to fewer permissions than the App has.
intro: Every agent pushes and opens PRs as the rhino-ai-agents App, and a ruleset on fcp's main decides what may merge. This lesson covers both halves: the identity (App, private key, short tokens) and the rule book (rulesets, required checks, bypass).

picture.caption: The broker turns the App's private key into a one-hour, one-repo token. The ruleset on main checks approvals and required checks before a person merges.

steps.text: the pod reads app_id and the private key; the VM never does
signs a JWT with the key and asks for an installation token for fcp only
returns a token that lives one hour with the narrowed permissions
asks the broker to push the branch and open the PR as rhino-ai-agents[bot]
requires 1 independent approval, green required checks, no force-push
approves and merges; the App is not a bypass actor and the broker refuses merge

p: A GitHub App is an identity that is not a person. It has an id and a private key.

It has a list of permissions it may ever use, and a list of repos it is installed on. When it acts, commits and PRs show rhino-ai-agents[bot] as the author. That lets rules treat its work differently from a person's.
G0-08 creates the App from the manifest below. Read the permission list slowly. contents and pull_requests write let it push and open PRs.
checks and actions read let it see CI results. metadata read is always required. Not in the list: workflows, administration, members.
sections.because: We give the App exactly these permissions for one reason. Without the workflows permission, GitHub refuses any push from it that changes .github/workflows, and that refusal is a wall we want.

code.text:
{
  "name": "rhino-ai-agents",
  "description": "Identity for Rhino's AI agents (Nova and the routines). The broker mints a 1-hour token per run for one repo.",
  "url": "https://github.com/RhinoHealth/ai-agents",
  "public": false,
  "hook_attributes": { "active": false },
  "default_events": [],
  "default_permissions": {
    "metadata": "read",
    "contents": "write",
    "pull_requests": "write",
    "checks": "read",
    "actions": "read"
  }
}

notes.text: Private: only RhinoHealth can install it. It is installed on fcp only, with 'Only select repositories'.
No webhook. Agents are triggered by Jira polling, Slack and small Actions, not by GitHub calling us.
This is the ceiling. A token minted later can ask for less, never for more.
contents: write lets the App push branches. It still cannot merge into main past the ruleset.
No workflows permission on purpose: a push that touches .github/workflows is refused by GitHub itself.

sections.h: A token for one hour and one repo
p: The App's private key never leaves the server side. It is stored in Vault at kvv2 infrastructure/ai-agents/github-app and read by the broker's pod. A pod is the running container of a service on our Kubernetes cluster (p5-1). To act, the broker signs a small JWT with the key and asks GitHub for an installation token. That token is a normal bearer token, valid for one hour.

At that moment you can narrow it: which repos, which permissions. A run that only needs to push and open a PR on fcp gets a token for fcp. It has contents and pull_requests write, and nothing else. The VM only ever sees this short token, through the broker.
sections.because: We mint a narrowed token per run because a leaked token should be useless an hour later. It should also be useless on any other repo.

notes.text: createAppAuth holds the key in memory and signs the JWT for you.
type: installation asks for a token that acts on the installed repos, as the bot.
repositoryNames narrows the token to fcp even if the App is installed on more repos later.
permissions narrows further. Asking for more than the App has fails; asking for less is the point.
expiresAt is about one hour out. The broker mints a fresh one for the next run.

callout.text: Inside a workflow the same thing is one step: actions/create-github-app-token with app-id, private-key and permission-contents: read. G1-03 and G2-09 use it for read-only tokens from a separate small App, so the agents' key stays with the broker alone.

sections.h: Rulesets: the rule book for main
p: A ruleset is a set of rules attached to branches that match a pattern. It replaces the older 'branch protection'. fcp already has one, main-branch-protection, id 5937570, but it is disabled. G0-02 turns it on with the API call below, run once by an org admin.
The call is a PUT with a JSON body. Read it as three parts: which branches, who may bypass, and the rules. This first block has the first two.
sections.because: We apply the ruleset with the API instead of clicking. The JSON can then be exported, reviewed and kept with the review-rules page.

code.file: run once by an org admin (from G0-02, part 1)
code.text:
# Run by an org admin. Agents never change rulesets.
# 5937570 is the existing, disabled "main-branch-protection" ruleset on fcp.
TEAM_ID=$(gh api orgs/RhinoHealth/teams/fcp-break-glass --jq .id)   # Tal and Nir

gh api -X PUT repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570 --input - <<EOF
{
  "name": "main-branch-protection",
  "target": "branch",
  "enforcement": "active",
  "conditions": { "ref_name": { "include": ["refs/heads/main"], "exclude": [] } },
  "bypass_actors": [
    { "actor_type": "Team", "actor_id": ${TEAM_ID}, "bypass_mode": "pull_request" }
  ],

notes.text: Rulesets cannot name single people as bypass actors, so G0-02 creates a team with Tal and Nir first.
PUT replaces the whole ruleset. --input - reads the JSON body from the heredoc that follows.
active turns it on. The other value, evaluate, only logs what would have been blocked.
Only main. Other branches stay free, which is where agents work.
pull_request mode: the team may bypass only through a PR, and GitHub logs every bypass.

p: The second block lists the rules. deletion and non_fast_forward stop anyone from deleting main or force-pushing over it. pull_request requires one approving review, drops approvals when new commits arrive, and requires the last push to be approved by someone else. required_status_checks names the checks that must be green.
sections.because: We require exactly one approval, with stale approvals dismissed. It is the smallest rule that makes a second person look at every change, from people and agents alike.

code.file: run once by an org admin (from G0-02, part 2)
code.text:
"rules": [
    { "type": "deletion" },
    { "type": "non_fast_forward" },
    { "type": "pull_request", "parameters": {
        "required_approving_review_count": 1,
        "dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push": true,
        "require_last_push_approval": true,
        "require_code_owner_review": false,
        "required_review_thread_resolution": false,
        "allowed_merge_methods": ["squash"] } },
    { "type": "required_status_checks", "parameters": {
        "strict_required_status_checks_policy": false,
        "required_status_checks": [
          { "context": "Cloud Unit Tests" },
          { "context": "Client Unit Tests" },
          { "context": "Frontend Unit Tests" } ] } }
  ]
}
EOF

notes.text: non_fast_forward is the force-push block. History on main can only grow.
A new commit after an approval needs a new approval. Otherwise an agent could push after the review.
Whoever pushed last cannot be the approver. G0-09 adds the stronger version for agent PRs.
No CODEOWNERS: fcp has none and the design keeps it that way; the one approval is the rule.
strict: false means the branch need not be rebased on the newest main before merge.
The context is the check's name exactly as GitHub shows it. Today all three jobs are called 'Unit Tests'; G0-02 renames them.

sections.h: Required checks: names must match, and skipped passes
p: A required check is matched by name. If the job is named 'Unit Tests' in three workflows, the ruleset cannot tell them apart. Say the workflow has a paths: filter and the PR does not touch those paths. Then the workflow never runs and the check stays pending forever, so the PR can never merge.

G0-02 fixes both: rename the jobs to 'Cloud Unit Tests', 'Client Unit Tests' and 'Frontend Unit Tests', and remove paths: filters. The check-changes job still skips the work with if:, and a skipped job counts as passing. For a reusable workflow the name is 'workflow name / job id', for example 'independent-approval / check'.

callout.text: The I&T gate e2e_tests and sdk-ci stay optional for now. The per-cloud QA locks make them too slow to require on every PR.

sections.h: Who merges, and who never does
p: Bypass actors are the only ones who can get past the rules, and only in the mode given. The App is deliberately not in the list, so even with contents: write it cannot merge an unapproved PR. G0-08 proves it: mint a test token and try; the merge must fail. The broker refuses the merge endpoint as well, so a person always merges.
Export the ruleset to JSON afterwards (gh api repos/RhinoHealth/fcp/rulesets/5937570). Keep it next to the review-rules page, so a change to it is a reviewed diff, not a click.

callout.text: Agents never change rulesets, never merge, and the App has no bypass. The requester never approves their own agent's PR; exactly one independent approval is the rule.

lab.title: Make a bot, mint a token, lock a branch
youNeed: actions-lab (public, so rulesets work on the free plan)

worked.do: In the browser: Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps, New GitHub App. Name lab-bot-<yourname>, any homepage URL, webhook off, permissions Contents: read and write, Pull requests: read and write. Create it, note the App ID, generate a private key (a .pem downloads).
worked.see: App ID shown on the App's page; a file like lab-bot.2026-10-13.private-key.pem in Downloads

worked.do: On the App's page: Install App, your account, Only select repositories, actions-lab. Then note the installation id from the URL (…/installations/<id>).
mkdir app-lab && cd app-lab && npm init -y && npm install @octokit/auth-app@8.1.0 @octokit/rest@22.0.1 tsx@4.20.5 && mv ~/Downloads/*.private-key.pem key.pem && echo key.pem >> .gitignore

Write mint.ts: import createAppAuth; read process.env.APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID and the key with readFileSync('key.pem','utf8'); call auth({ type: 'installation', installationId, repositoryNames: ['actions-lab'], permissions: { contents: 'write', pull_requests: 'write' } }); print expiresAt and the token's first 8 characters only.
Extend mint.ts to call new Octokit({ auth: token }).rest.apps.listReposAccessibleToInstallation() and print the repo names.
cd ../actions-lab && git switch -c try-merge && echo x >> README.md && git commit -am 'Try' && git push -u origin try-merge && gh pr create --fill && gh pr merge --squash
worked.see:
X Pull request #N is not mergeable: the base branch policy prohibits the merge.
(1 approving review required; required status check 'hello' …)

lab.faded: Export your ruleset with gh api repos/seanazu/actions-lab/rulesets/<id> > ruleset.json and read it. Then change required_approving_review_count to 0 in the file and send it back with gh api -X PUT … --input ruleset.json. The merge command from the last step should now wait only for the hello check; run it and watch.
lab.alone: Take the bot token from mint.ts. Use Octokit to open a PR from a new branch (pulls.create), then try pulls.merge on it. Read the error, then add the App as a bypass actor (actor_type Integration, actor_id = your App ID) and try again. Remove the bypass afterwards and delete key.pem; our real App never has a bypass.
lab.done: You minted a one-hour token that lists only actions-lab. A ruleset blocked an unapproved squash merge, and you saw the error text that an agent would see.

quiz.q: The App has contents: write. Can a run with its token merge a PR into fcp's main?

options.why: The ruleset applies to the App like to anyone else. Without an approval and green checks GitHub refuses the merge.

options.text: No: the ruleset needs an approval and the App is not a bypass actor; the broker also refuses the merge endpoint.
options.why: Two walls, one in GitHub and one in the broker, so a person always merges.

options.text: Only if the PR was opened by the same App.
options.why: Who opened the PR changes nothing about merge rights.

quiz.q: Why does G0-02 rename the three 'Unit Tests' jobs and remove paths: filters?

options.text: To make the Actions tab easier to read.
options.why: Nice, but not the reason. The ruleset matches checks by name and cannot tell three identical names apart.

options.text: Because required checks are matched by name, and a workflow filtered out by paths: never reports, so the PR stays blocked.
options.why: Unique names make the check requirable; dropping paths: makes it always report, with if: skipping the work when nothing changed.

options.text: Because rulesets only allow three required checks.
options.why: There is no such limit; the three are the unit-test jobs that are fast enough to require.

quiz.q: Where does the rhino-ai-agents private key live, and who reads it?

options.text: In the sandbox VM, so the agent can push on its own.
options.why: No keys in the VM is a wall. The VM gets only a one-hour token through the broker.

options.text: In a repo secret in fcp.
options.why: fcp's workflows must not be able to act as the agents' identity; that key belongs to the broker alone.

options.text: In Vault at infrastructure/ai-agents/github-app, read by the broker's pod.
options.why: The broker signs the JWT and mints narrowed installation tokens from there; the downloaded .pem is deleted.

words.plain: A non-person identity with an id, a private key, a permission ceiling and a list of repos it is installed on.
A one-hour bearer token minted from the App's key for one installation, narrowable to fewer repos and permissions.
The number GitHub gives when the App is installed on an account; the broker needs it to mint tokens.
Rules attached to branches that match a pattern: approvals, required checks, no force-push, no delete.
A check named in the ruleset that must be green (or skipped) before merge.
A team, role or App allowed past the ruleset, in a given mode, with every bypass logged.

tickets.why: Creating the App from the manifest, storing the key in Vault and proving the App cannot merge is this lesson's first half.
Turning on the ruleset with required unit-test checks and the break-glass team is the second half.
The independent-approval check becomes a required check by its exact 'independent-approval / check' name.
The metrics job reads GitHub with a separate read-only App through create-github-app-token.

remember: Agents act as an App with one-hour, one-repo tokens minted by the broker. A ruleset on main needs one independent approval and green named checks, and the App has no bypass.
